title: Pendulum, 60 cm

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a school practical: true length 0.60 m, g = 9.81 m/s²)

reference.basis: plain white sheet is standard A4 paper long side

slow_motion.evidence: no captions or indicators of slow motion; motion looks real-time

subjects.description: small orange spherical bob on a thin black string

observation.what_happens: An orange ball suspended by a string from a fixed support swings side to side in a vertical plane. It moves continuously through the bottom of its arc, starting displaced to the right and oscillating left and right for the duration of the clip.

calibration.note: white paper = 0.297 m (plain white sheet is standard A4 paper long side) spans 170 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: white paper = 0.297 m (plain white sheet is standard A4 paper long side) spans 170 px in SAM's mask, known to ±6%
pendulum length L = 0.575 m, measured from the radius of the swing with the ruler: hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Theta oscillates about zero at ~0.17 rad with near-constant radius ~0.575 m and ~1.5 s period, matching a simple pendulum of the given length. Amplitude decays only slightly over 5.2 s, suggesting weak air damping. Candidates therefore go from ideal undamped to linear viscous to quadratic aerodynamic drag while holding L fixed to measure g.

caveats: Scale from paper width is known to only a few percent, so gravity inherits that uncertainty.
Length was held fixed from video measurement; any error there shifts gravity.
Linear viscous drag fits almost as well, so the exact type of air resistance is not firmly settled.
critique.finding: The ball swings as a pendulum pulled down by gravity {g} while quadratic air drag of strength {k} slowly shrinks each swing.
critique.headline: Swinging ball loses energy slowly to air drag.
critique.why_it_won: It captures the way fast swings lose extra energy that simple viscous slowing underestimates.

headline: Swinging ball loses energy slowly to air drag.
finding: The ball swings as a pendulum pulled down by gravity 9.4 ± 0.56 m/s² while quadratic air drag of strength 0.0495 ± 0.0017 1/rad slowly shrinks each swing.

eyeball.confidence: low-medium: length from paper scale ~0.5 m, period timed over ~5-6 swings in 8 s; drag decay very small so k only order-of-magnitude
eyeball.law_in_words: small-angle simple pendulum T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) with angular equation theta_ddot + (g/L) sin theta + k |theta_dot| theta_dot = 0 for quadratic air drag
